objective: Remove RLS-bypassing TRUNCATE, TRIGGER and REFERENCES grants from anonymous and ordinary authenticated roles on all existing public PostgreSQL tables, preserve DML and maintain ongoing security scan detection. Apply same ACL correction to the dedicated Quiz database without changing its login and answer RPCs.

Only two current SECURITY DEFINER routines issue TRUNCATE on pg_temp. Existing service_role/default finance RLS must remain intact. Full exact SQL executed BEGIN/ROLLBACK on production main and verified 0 residual grants plus retained service and client DML privileges; post rollback counts restored 368/380. Dedicated Quiz read-only: 23/23 public RLS, 5 anon TRUNCATE and 16 authenticated TRUNCATE grants; exact Quiz-only migration trial completed in BEGIN/ROLLBACK, preserving all three existing login/answer RPC signatures.
chosenApproach: Revoke only TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES on public existing ordinary/partitioned tables for PUBLIC,anon,authenticated; preserve normal DML, service role, and RLS; remove unsafe postgres default grants and extend private 15-minute metadata-only scanner.
selectionRationale: Smallest privilege correction. Avoid blanket ALL revocation that could break normal app queries. Authenticated clients never legitimately issue DDL. The platform-owned supabase_admin default ACL is not writable with postgres membership and is monitored for regression.
alternativeApproaches: Full revoke all table privileges and selectively rebuild grants: rejected due app regression risk.
Ignore table permissions because PostgREST lacks TRUNCATE HTTP endpoint: rejected; RLS bypass privileges remain unnecessarily exposed.
Alter provider-owned supabase_admin default privileges without role membership: rejected by least privilege.
